observation_summary: The compiler incorrectly flags variables defined in a catch block as 'undefined' because it fails to recognize the catch block as a valid scope or assignment context for those variables.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves adding 'case Token.CATCH:' to a switch statement in GlobalNamespace. This is a procedural correction to the logic that determines whether a name is 'set' (assigned/defined). By including the CATCH token, the compiler correctly identifies that variables within a catch block are defined, thus preventing the false 'JSC_UNDEFINED_NAME' warning. This is an algorithmic fix to the name-tracking logic, not a design-level capability gap or a simple initialization error.
evidence_used: The fix adds 'case Token.CATCH:' to a switch statement in GlobalNamespace.
The bug report states the compiler doesn't model variables introduced by a catch block correctly.
The failing test 'testGlobalCatch' confirms that the compiler incorrectly warns about 'e' being undefined in a catch block.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves a switch case, it is not a guard or validation check; it is an update to the logic that tracks variable definitions.
This is a local procedural fix within the existing name-tracking algorithm, not a design-level capability omission.
